FR-L2: partly built: every project ledger is an append-only JSONL file written under a lock (kernel/ledgerstore.py), and each state change the kernel makes appends its transition, signed with the person where a person made it (FR-L2-AC-1, AC-2); not built: the state itself is kept in JSON documents the kernel rewrites in place beside the ledger (project.json, canon/*.json, contract.json, tasks.json), so the ledger records transitions but is not the state's source and nothing rebuilds state from it; nothing enforces that only kernel/ writes (the cockpit writes its own files directly: layouts, kept heads, exports, job logs); and some state is written with no transition: the factory's own canon is created on first use with no ledger record (kernel/learn.py factory_project, reached by GET /api/dashboard), Canon.note writes exchange notes unrecorded, and GET /api/projects/{pid}/pack writes packs.json and the release's capability-pack.json. Building it would mean making each state file a projection of the ledger with a replay that rebuilds it, and a check that refuses project writes from outside the kernel.
FR-L3: partly built: a ledger head can be taken (LedgerStore.head) and checked against (FR-L1-AC-4); the cockpit keeps each project's last verified head outside the project's folder and catches a rewritten tail by it (FR-L3-AC-1); a release's capability pack carries the ledger head it was built at (FR-L3-AC-2); not built: no head is ever signed (no signing key or signer exists; the pack says 'not signed: no signer configured'), and no head is anchored off this machine (no remote git ref, transparency log or Gnomon [audit.anchor] use): the kept heads sit in the same factory home as the ledgers, so whoever can rewrite a ledger can rewrite cockpit/heads.json too. Building it would take a signer configured by a person (for example an SSH or minisign key outside the factory home), a signed head record per gate or release, and a push of each signed head to an external store the factory cannot rewrite.
FR-N1: partly built: the cockpit's JSON API (cockpit/server.py) serves the factory's read models over loopback behind a session token, and every read but one writes nothing (FR-N1-AC-1); every write that records state carries a named person and persona and is refused for a non-person (FR-N1-AC-2); not built: there is no server-sent event stream (no text/event-stream route; the page fetches on demand, and only its live panel polls the live read model every 5 s while visible); POST /api/projects/{pid}/advance takes no person and starts the pipeline as a job, so it is a write path that is not signed; GET /api/projects/{pid}/pack writes on a read (the pack's version in packs.json, the release's capability-pack.json and a pack_versioned ledger record); and the signed writes are wider than decisions: signals, comments, change requests, embeds, layouts, autonomy caps and evidence exports are signed writes that are not Inbox decisions. Building it would take an event route streaming ledger appends per project, a person required on advance, and the pack built when a release is recorded instead of when it is read.
